motion: Is belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God rational given alleged gratuitous evil, salvation confusion, rationality, design, and morality?

lockedRoutes.description: Show that belief in the specified all-powerful, all-loving God is not proportioned to available reason and evidence because central divine attributes conflict with suffering, confused revelation, or rival explanations.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if one or more undefeated considerations make belief in this specified God materially less rational than withholding belief, even if some creator hypothesis remains possible.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative evidence and unresolved contradictions make belief in the specified God irrational.

centralBridges.description: Apparently gratuitous suffering is strongly improbable under an all-powerful and all-loving God.
Evolutionary and natural explanations undercut claimed theistic advantages concerning cognition, design, and morality.
Grounding goodness in God does not escape arbitrariness or an independent standard of goodness.
High-stakes salvation requirements are confused and supported by culturally variable revelation claims.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The evil-God parity shows that a merely possible theodicy does not establish rational probability.
Religious and moral disagreement weakens claims of clear, reliable divine disclosure.

lockedRoutes.description: Show that belief in God is rational because theism offers a cumulative explanation of reliable reason, life-permitting order, objective morality, purpose, and the ultimate treatment of suffering.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cumulative theistic explanation remains reasonably warranted after objections, without needing to prove that every instance of suffering or every scriptural question is fully resolved.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative explanatory case makes belief in God more rational than its principal alternatives.

centralBridges.description: A rational creator better explains trustworthy minds and an intelligible universe than unguided naturalism.
Life-permitting fine-tuning is substantially more probable under intelligent design than under chance.
Objective moral value is best grounded in the necessarily good character of a personal creator.
Suffering is serious counterevidence but does not defeat theism given afterlife, theodicy, and divine participation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Guided evolution can preserve evolutionary mechanisms while explaining truth-directed cognitive capacities.
Genre-sensitive interpretation permits rational confidence in biblical revelation without literalizing every story.

lockedSections.title: Gratuitous evil and theodicy
lockedSections.rationale: The specified divine attributes and the scale of apparently purposeless suffering form the pro side's principal objection and elicit the con side's most direct defensive case.

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: Mass extinction, disease, predation, parasites, and atrocity appear gratuitous; insisting that every case serves a greater good is no more rational than protecting an evil-God hypothesis with merely possible stories.

sourceSpan.excerpt: gratuitous evil ... does not serve any greater purpose ... mere possibility doesn't imply high probability ... this is a parity of the irrationality of Abrahamic theism

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: Suffering is powerful counterevidence but not a defeater because Christianity affirms that the world is not as it should be, includes an afterlife, has serious free-will and soul-making accounts, and depicts God as participating in suffering.

sourceSpan.excerpt: the evidence of suffering and evil ... is probably the strongest counterevidence ... but I don't think it's a defeater ... free will defense Soul making theodicy

lockedSections.title: Evolution and cognitive reliability
lockedSections.rationale: The con side argues that unguided evolution undermines trust in reason, while the pro side disputes both the scope of the target and the claimed separation of survival from truth.

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: The argument overgeneralizes from naturalism to atheism and wrongly infers global unreliability, because broadly accurate beliefs are often adaptively valuable even though evolved cognition remains fallible.

sourceSpan.excerpt: that's not an argument in favor of theism ... most atheists don't actually affirm naturalism ... evolution ... is going to select the things that are broadly true

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: If minds arise through mindless unguided processes selecting advantageous behavior rather than truth, naturalism undercuts confidence in cognition, whereas a rational creator supplies a basis for trustworthy minds.

sourceSpan.excerpt: natural selection does not directly select for True beliefs but rather for advantageous behaviors ... if God exists there is an intelligent Creator ... our minds being rational

lockedSections.title: Fine-tuning, design, and evolutionary explanation
lockedSections.rationale: The con side presents fine-tuning as strong design evidence, while the pro side later argues that developed natural explanations substantially reduce older design-based inferences.

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: Design inference was more reasonable before evolutionary evidence supplied a detailed natural account of biological complexity; current evidence therefore undercuts broad appeals from complexity or human form to deliberate creation.

sourceSpan.excerpt: before Evolution was put on the board ... it was very hard to look around the world ... Evolution has made it very clear that if God exists he chose to use Evolution

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: Numerous life-permitting physical constants occupy extremely narrow ranges, making intelligent design far more probable than their occurrence by chance.

sourceSpan.excerpt: the Discovery by physicists that our universe is finely tuned for life ... for all practical intents and purposes impossible ... a super intellect has monkeyed with the physics

lockedSections.title: Objective morality and the Euthyphro dilemma
lockedSections.rationale: The con side treats objective moral value as evidence for God, while the pro side challenges both evolutionary alternatives and the coherence of identifying divine character with goodness.

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: Evolution of cooperative social groups explains moral intuitions and persistent disagreement under either atheism or theism, so those intuitions do not uniquely support an objective divine moral law.

sourceSpan.excerpt: under a theist or an atheistic view evolution provides a very simple explanation for the moral feelings that we have ... explains why there's so much moral disagreement

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: Saying that God is goodness merely relocates the Euthyphro dilemma: either divine character aligns with an independent good or divine character defines good and remains arbitrary.

sourceSpan.excerpt: it's just kicking the can down the road ... is God good because what he aligns with is some goodness ... or is he good because he defines what good is

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: Objective wrongs such as racism, bullying, and sexual abuse are best explained by an objective moral law grounded in God, because impersonal physical reality cannot itself generate obligations.

sourceSpan.excerpt: some things such as bullying or racism or sexual abuse are objectively wrong ... the existence of this objective moral law points us to the existence of God

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: The Euthyphro dilemma is false because God neither follows an external good nor arbitrarily invents goodness; God's character is itself the personal source of objective goodness.

sourceSpan.excerpt: the answer to the Euthyphro dilemma ... God commands what he does not because it is good but because he is the good ... ultimately sourced in the person of God

lockedSections.title: Salvation confusion and revelation
lockedSections.rationale: The pro side argues that culturally variable, disputed revelation is incompatible with high-stakes salvation requirements, while both sides address how scriptural claims should be evaluated.

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: An all-loving God would not attach grave postmortem consequences to accepting disputed propositions when religious communities disagree about salvation and the supposed evidential hoop is difficult to identify.

sourceSpan.excerpt: most Christians let alone Muslims and Jews can't even agree on what's necessary for salvation ... those of us ... who cannot see the hoop ... be eternally punished

proMoves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
proMoves.proposition: Some biblical history may be credible, but historical existence does not establish resurrection or miracles, and an all-loving God would not require belief in claims that largely track cultural upbringing.

sourceSpan.excerpt: some of the stories in the Bible are true but plenty of them are not ... it's a mistake to think that because he existed he resurrected ... born and bred to take it seriously

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: Human beings exist intentionally because God wanted them, and divine purpose is compatible with God using guided evolutionary mechanisms rather than direct creation.

sourceSpan.excerpt: we're here on purpose because somebody God wanted us to be here ... hugely open to the idea that God could have used mechanisms of natural selection ... guided Evolution

conMoves.speaker: Simon Edwards
conMoves.proposition: Rational interpretation of the Bible distinguishes historical records, poetry, and parables, so accepting biblical revelation does not require treating every narrated story as literal history.

sourceSpan.excerpt: it's a collection of different books and some books are clearly historical records ... some books are poetry ... they were stories, parables
